left.tested_scope: Crash-consistent OUTER evaluation state machine with durable intents, stable per-cell logical IDs, reconcile-before-execute, immutable outcomes, deterministic certification, and six real SIGKILL recovery boundaries in a SQLite-backed provider simulator.

right.tested_scope: Exact post-hoc executor-interface sensitivity test for one frozen AWM port in the paper's native function-calling executor. The literal WebArena <think>/<action> envelope was preserved although the executor expected native function calls: across 540 rollouts, 380 emitted textual action blocks and exactly those 380 executed zero real tools. The literal port had utility 0.319, exposure 0.299, ASR 0.195 and unauthorized-state change 0.217. Reusing the same three workflows while removing only four literal tag strings raised utility to 0.756, exposure to 0.909, ASR to 0.575 and unauthorized-state change to 0.714, while zero-real-tool-call rate fell from 0.704 to 0.046. This establishes interface mismatch as the dominant confound for this tested port, not a general property of AWM across executors.

comparison.semantic_overlap: Both candidates show that evaluation claims can be invalid when the actual execution path is not faithfully realized or observed. The overlap is limited to execution-path validity: the left is a crash-consistency/idempotent-recovery mechanism that deliberately survives six process-death boundaries while preserving effect identity and outcome reconciliation, whereas FE-357 is a sensitivity test showing that a serialization/interface mismatch suppresses real tool execution and can make a system appear both less capable and safer.
distinguishing_scope: terminal_outer_sigkill_reference tests recovery correctness after real process death using durable intents, stable logical IDs, reconcile-before-execute, immutable outcomes and deterministic certification; it does not test action-envelope compatibility, textual-vs-native function-call mismatch, or safety metrics under suppressed tool execution.

FE-357 tests whether the evaluator/executor interface itself prevents real tool use and quantifies utility, exposure, ASR, unauthorized-state change and zero-real-tool-call sensitivity when only literal tag strings are removed; it does not test crash recovery, durable effect intent, SIGKILL resilience, idempotent reconcile-before-execute, or OUTER WAL semantics.

phase1_hard_gates.reason: This is pairwise deduplication evidence only. The left tested scope relies on local subprocess/SIGKILL execution plus a SQLite-backed provider simulator, while FE-357 is an empirical post-hoc executor-interface sensitivity test rather than a complete scheduled-Chat-native dependency-elimination route. The pair establishes no accepted end-to-end Phase-1 route.
